reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a passive-income front-running bot that requires connecting MetaMask, deploying a contract, paying gas fees, and funding it with Ether. It claims the bot can profit by placing another user's transaction between its trades to capture slippage, with reported earnings of about 1.17 Ether and usually more than two Ether per week. The records do not independently verify the balances, code behavior, or completed results.

citations.quote: This YouTube video tutorial I'll be explaining to you an easy method to make passive income using Uniswap.
So to start off, you'll need to have MetaMask installed and connected to the Ethereum mainnet.
click the deploy button to publish our contract to the Ethereum blockchain
the next step is to fund our contract with some ethers to be able to snipe liquidity
our transaction to be processed first and then will also send a sell order within the same block.

opening.argument: The presentation does not promise an automatic or risk-free return. It expressly acknowledges that results vary and that the activity can lose money: profitability is not constant, and gas fees affect the outcome. That qualification matters because the speaker presents the claimed returns as a personal experience, not as a guaranteed result for every viewer. A careful reading therefore supports a technical explanation with material risk disclosure rather than a deceptive assurance of income.

citations.quote: Sometimes its not always profitable and profits fluctuate week to week
all of that in the same block
usually I make 2 plus ethereum a week

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes the funding and deployment steps, but those steps are disclosed openly rather than concealed. Its own quotations establish the described mechanism, not deception or a guarantee. The earnings discussion is also presented with an explicit qualification that profitability fluctuates, which undercuts the claim that viewers are being promised certain returns.

citations.quote: You can fund the contract with whatever amount you want
Sometimes its not always profitable and profits fluctuate week to week

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A risk disclaimer does not neutralize the central solicitation. The speaker still calls this an easy passive-income method and reports substantial personal gains, while directing viewers to fund a contract. Saying results fluctuate concedes uncertainty but leaves the core income pitch intact; it does not show that the claimed bot returns are independently verified.

citations.quote: an easy method to make passive income using Uniswap
the contract is funded
usually I make 2 plus ethereum a week

opening.argument: The video's dominant form is a technical tutorial. It explains a blockchain concept, shows how to create and compile a Solidity file, connects Remix to MetaMask, and demonstrates deployment and contract controls. The explanatory spreadsheet is explicitly presented as an example of front running, while the surrounding material walks through software and blockchain operations. That structure is consistent with education or a demonstration of a claimed technique, not necessarily an endorsement that viewers will safely earn money.

citations.quote: This YouTube video tutorial I'll be explaining to you
Now as you can see, the contract is built for the 0.6.6 version of Solidity.
now we deploy this to our wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling something a tutorial does not change what the tutorial instructs viewers to do. The steps go beyond abstract education: viewers are told to deploy a contract, fund it with Ether, start it, and withdraw funds. The example is not merely historical commentary because the speaker presents an operational workflow and reports purported profits from using it.

citations.quote: the next step is to fund our contract with some ethers to be able to snipe liquidity
The last step is to click start
The bot will then exit the liquidity pool and will return back to the wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The software instructions are not neutral merely because they include code and compiler settings. The tutorial explicitly describes using a funded contract to front-run other transactions and then showcases claimed returns. The label 'example' on a diagram does not establish that the operational instructions are only academic or that the demonstrated strategy is safe.

citations.quote: This is going to allow us to sniff the pending transactions
bot made over the 10 hours

opening.argument: The material can also be read as a software and operational service demonstration: it uses public blockchain tools, a coding environment, a wallet interface, and a contract explorer. It does not describe recruiting others, collecting credentials, or requiring a downline. Nor does it state that returns are guaranteed; instead, it says results fluctuate. The evidence therefore shows a user-operated technical workflow and performance claims, but does not establish the broader hallmarks of a deceptive sales scheme.

citations.quote: Remikx is web application that allows us to develop, deploy, compile and launch smart contracts
Sometimes its not always profitable and profits fluctuate week to week
We can check that by following our contract address on etherscan.io

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of recruitment or credential collection is beside the point when the described mechanism requires viewers to put Ether into a contract. The speaker expressly says that more funding enables larger front-runs and reports profits from the bot. This is not ordinary retail commerce merely because public tools are used; the financial inducement is the central activity.

citations.quote: the more you put in, the larger the transaction you'll be able to front-run
the contract is funded
the bot made for me

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a downline or password request does not make a funded-return scheme ordinary commerce. The relevant mechanism is the request to transfer Ether to a contract in pursuit of claimed profits. The fluctuation disclaimer does not cure the persuasive performance claims, including the statement that the speaker usually makes more than two Ether weekly.
